description: Create an order with line items. Idempotent by externalId — use a stable unique id such as 'mcp-<uuid>' (re-sending returns the existing order). Enforces the workspace plan limit; the result echoes the operating workspace. Items snapshot productName/sku/unitPrice; use search_products first to quote real products.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code for the order (uppercase, e.g. UAH). Default UAH.

customer.description: Optional buyer snapshot (name/email/phone, or a storefront customer externalId). Omit for an anonymous order.

delivery.description: How the buyer asked to receive the order: carrier, branch/courier/pickup, branch text, recipient, cash-on-delivery and a delivery note. This is the buyer's choice at checkout — it does not dispatch anything. Record what actually ships with POST /orders/{externalId}/shipments.

branch.description: Branch or parcel locker as the buyer named it, e.g. "відділення №5" or "поштомат 12345". Free text: the CRM resolves it against the live branch list of the carrier when creating a waybill.

branchRef.description: The carrier's own identifier for the branch or parcel locker, as returned by GET /api/v1/carriers/{carrier}/warehouses. The same value the shipment-label endpoint calls warehouseRef. Sent, this removes all guessing; omitted, the CRM falls back to matching `branch` as text.

building.description: House number for courier delivery, structured rather than inside the address line because carriers validate it on its own (Nova Poshta accepts up to 11 characters matching digits plus an optional Cyrillic letter or block, e.g. "12Б" or "12/4").

carrier.description: Carrier slug the buyer chose, from GET /capabilities (e.g. "nova_poshta", "ukrposhta", "pickup"). This is a preference, not a dispatch — the shipment endpoint still records what actually ships.

cityRef.description: The carrier's own identifier for the destination city, as returned by GET /api/v1/carriers/{carrier}/cities. Required alongside branchRef or streetRef for a waybill to be created from the order alone.

cod.description: True when the buyer pays on delivery (cash on delivery).

comment.description: Delivery note from the buyer, e.g. "дзвонити після 18:00". Not the order notes.

flat.description: Apartment or office number for courier delivery.

method.description: How the parcel reaches the buyer: "branch" (carrier office/locker), "courier" (to the address) or "pickup" (buyer collects from you).

phone.description: Recipient phone, when it differs from the buyer's own contact phone.

recipientName.description: Who receives the parcel, when that is not the buyer (a gift, an office).

streetRef.description: The carrier's own identifier for the street, as returned by GET /api/v1/carriers/{carrier}/streets. Courier delivery only; pair it with `building`.

discountAmount.description: Money taken off by the promo code, in the order currency. A sum, not a percent: a percent at order level is ambiguous (before or after line discounts, with shipping or without). Does NOT change total — send the total the buyer actually paid.

externalId.description: A stable unique id for this order in your system — the idempotency key. Re-sending the same externalId returns the existing order instead of creating a duplicate (e.g. 'mcp-<uuid>').

items.description: Order line items (1-100). Each snapshots productName/sku/unitPrice.

discount.description: Percentage discount on this line (0-100). Default 0.

productName.description: Line item name, snapshotted onto the order. Use search_products to quote a real catalog product's name. Required.

unitPrice.description: Price per unit in the order currency, as a decimal (e.g. 199.99). Snapshotted onto the line.

notes.description: Internal note stored on the order. For a delivery instruction from the buyer use delivery.comment instead.

promoCode.description: The promo code the storefront applied to this order, recorded as-is. The CRM never validates or computes it — the cart owns that — but storing it is what makes 'did that campaign pay for itself?' answerable later.
